title: The emergence and evolution of a referential code in populations of bee-like agents
one_sentence: A colony simulation shows how embodied geometry and sender–receiver coupling can support emergence and transition from iconic pointing to an abstract gravity-referenced directional code.
problem: Under what ecological and bodily constraints can a referential code emerge and change without a catastrophic loss of communication?
method: Evolutionary colony simulation across food ecologies, comb geometry, mutation scales, correlated sender/receiver mutation, multiple seeds, sensitivity analyses, and held-out confirmation.
findings: Direct pointing emerges only in an intermediate ecology where signals are both available and useful.

A transition to a gravity-referenced code is feasible under sufficient vertical-comb benefit and coordinated sender/receiver change; the strongest held-out setting produced stable transitions in 91/100 and 92/100 runs without nonviable colonies.
real_contribution: Makes bodily substrate and coordinated encoder/decoder change explicit mechanisms of convention emergence and code transition.
biggest_weakness: Feasibility simulation rather than a probability estimate or behavioral study; permissive evolutionary assumptions, direction-only signals, and no human or robot partners.
claim_boundary: Does not establish interaction-timescale human–AI grounding, repair, partner specificity, multimodal integration, or socially relational meaning.
why_researcher_should_care: Suggests a falsifiable AMSC manipulation: change embodied affordances mid-interaction and measure whether both partners can renegotiate a code without breakdown.
evidence_notes: Open arXiv HTML/PDF inspected; v1 submitted 2026-08-26.
Evolutionary adaptation is treated as a theory neighbor, not a direct human–AI result.
